summary: Security review of the parking system architecture. The design includes JWT-based authentication, role-based access control (driver/admin), and mock payments. No secrets are present in the repository. Key risks include lack of rate limiting on login, potential IDOR in session/notification endpoints if ownership is not enforced, and absence of input validation details for geo-coordinates and polygons.

findings.title: Potential IDOR in session and notification endpoints
findings.description: Endpoints such as /sessions/{session_id}/end and /notifications/{notification_id}/read accept resource IDs in the path. If the backend does not verify that the authenticated user owns the resource, an attacker could manipulate session or notification IDs to access or modify other users' data.

findings.title: No rate limiting on /auth/login
findings.description: The login endpoint lacks documented rate limiting or account lockout mechanisms, which could allow brute-force attacks against user credentials.

findings.title: Input validation for geo-coordinates and polygons
findings.description: The architecture accepts latitude/longitude and polygon data (GeoJSON/WKT) without specifying validation rules. Malformed or malicious geo-data could lead to injection, DoS, or logic errors in zone matching.

findings.title: JWT configuration details not specified
findings.description: The architecture references JWT tokens but does not specify token expiration, refresh strategy, or signing algorithm. Proper configuration is critical to prevent token replay or forgery.

findings.title: No secrets in repository
findings.description: No hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credentials were found in the provided architecture or code artifacts. Secrets should be managed via environment variables or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Role-based access control implemented
findings.description: Admin endpoints are protected with role checks (403 errors), and user endpoints are scoped to the authenticated user. This mitigates unauthorized access to administrative functions.

findings.title: Mock payment system
findings.description: Payments are mocked and do not involve real financial transactions. This reduces the risk of financial fraud but means that payment-related security controls (e.g., PCI-DSS) are not applicable in the current scope.
